findings.topic: 4. AXES — ER-6/ER-8/ER-9 for #325
findings.fact: docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md: ER-6 — 'A reference can hold at most one active direct rights-tier grant per entity. Granting a new direct tier ... retires (soft-deletes) the old one — even via a bare, independent POST carrying no prior _id.' ER-8 — the ER-6 replace is strictly same-entity/same-reference, does not extend to parent→child propagation. ER-9 — the replacement is non-monotonic: 'a lower tier granted second retires a higher one, not just the reverse ... a later explicit lower-tier grant to that same caller on that same entity silently demotes the creator from owner — the replace happens with no error and no notice.' For #325: a double-tap on conductor/admin/librarian add-or-remove fires two concurrent direct-grant writes for the SAME reference on the SAME entity; ER-6/ER-9 mean the SECOND write to land — regardless of which tap the user intended as final — silently WINS and retires the first, with no error surfaced by the platform. The pending guard is the only thing preventing a genuinely ambiguous outcome (not just a wasted duplicate request), which is exactly why #325 calls this 'correctness, not cosmetics.'
findings.evidence: Read docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md lines 227-238 (ER-6, ER-8, ER-9 definitions and qualifications)
